description:
The Establishment of 12 Milch Animal Farms scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2021. 

This initiative aims to enhance milk production in the country. 

The scheme is part of the larger effort to promote dairy farming and improve the livelihood of farmers. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to establish 12 milch animal farms across various states. 

These farms are intended to increase the availability of high-quality milk. 

The target is to produce approximately 1.2 lakh liters of milk per day from these farms. 

This initiative is expected to benefit around 10,000 farmers directly. 

The scheme also aims to create employment opportunities in rural areas. 

The estimated cost for establishing each farm is around INR 1 crore. 

The total investment for the establishment of all 12 farms is approximately INR 12 crores. 

The scheme is designed to provide financial assistance to farmers for purchasing milch animals. 

Farmers can receive up to 50 percent of the cost of the animals as a subsidy. 

This subsidy can amount to INR 25,000 per animal. 

The eligibility criteria for farmers include being a resident of the state where the farm is established. 

Farmers must also possess a minimum of 2 acres of agricultural land. 

The age limit for applicants is set at 18 years and above. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required for farmers to apply. 

The application process involves several steps. 

Interested farmers must first visit the local animal husbandry department office. 

They need to obtain the application form for the scheme. 

Farmers must fill out the application form with accurate details. 

The required documents include proof of identity, land ownership documents, and a bank account statement. 

Once the application is completed, it must be submitted to the local animal husbandry department. 

The department will review the applications and verify the details provided. 

After verification, eligible farmers will receive an approval notification. 

The disbursement of funds will occur within 30 days of approval. 

Farmers will then be able to purchase milch animals using the subsidy amount. 

The scheme also includes provisions for training farmers in dairy management. 

Training sessions will cover animal nutrition, health care, and milk production techniques. 

The training will be conducted by experts from the animal husbandry department. 

The timeline for establishing the farms is set for completion within two years from the approval date. 

Each farm is expected to house around 100 to 150 milch animals. 

The breeds of milch animals will primarily include Jersey and Holstein Friesian. 

These breeds are known for their high milk yield and quality. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The contact details for the department can be found on the official government website. 

Farmers can also reach out to local veterinary officers for assistance. 

The scheme aims to improve the overall dairy infrastructure in the country. 

It is expected to enhance the income of farmers by providing a steady source of revenue. 

The initiative aligns with the National Dairy Plan launched in 2012. 

The National Dairy Plan aims to increase milk production in India by 50 percent by 2025. 

The establishment of these farms is a crucial step towards achieving that goal. 

The scheme also addresses the nutritional needs of the population. 

Increased milk production will contribute to better health and nutrition among citizens. 

The government has set a target to increase per capita availability of milk to 1.5 liters per day by 2025. 

The scheme is expected to play a significant role in achieving this target. 

Moreover, the initiative will help in reducing the dependency on imported dairy products. 

It will also contribute to the self-sufficiency of the dairy sector in India. 

The establishment of milch animal farms will promote sustainable dairy farming practices. 

Farmers will be encouraged to adopt modern technologies in dairy farming. 

The scheme will also focus on improving the quality of milk produced. 

Quality control measures will be implemented to ensure safe and hygienic milk production. 

The government will monitor the progress of the farms regularly. 

Periodic assessments will be conducted to evaluate the performance of the farms. 

The success of the scheme will be measured based on milk production levels and farmer incomes. 

The scheme is expected to have a multiplier effect on the rural economy. 

Increased milk production will lead to the growth of related industries. 

These include feed production, veterinary services, and milk processing. 

The government aims to create a robust dairy ecosystem through this initiative. 

Overall, the Establishment of 12 Milch Animal Farms scheme represents a significant investment in the dairy sector. 

It reflects the government's commitment to improving farmers' livelihoods and enhancing food security. 

The scheme is a vital component of India's agricultural and rural development strategy. 

By focusing on dairy farming, the government aims to empower farmers and promote rural development. 

This initiative is poised to make a lasting impact on the dairy industry in India.
